traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 1, 2nd ed., 1959), family 276 Polygonaceae: herbs, shrubs or climbers, rarely trees; leaves alternate, rarely opposite, the stalk's base often widened into a papery sheath round the stem (the ochrea, read here as its stipules); flowers small, regular; 3 to 6 sepals, often growing papery in fruit, and no petals, read as tepals; stamens usually 6 to 9; ovary superior, of one cell with one ovule; fruit a three-angled or two-sided nut, read as an achene.

traits.rosette.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Polygonaceae: whether the leaves gather in rosettes (character 22), coded usually no rosette, often a basal rosette. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.phyllotaxis_pattern.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 381, 383, family Polygonaceae: phyllotaxis pattern spiral, usually; read as {"spiral": "usually"}.

traits.leaf_division.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 381, 383, family Polygonaceae: leaf division simple; read as "simple".
